items.title: Headlines for October 28, 2026 | Democracy Now!
items.excerpt: ## Political Gridlock in Israel After No Clear Winner Emerges from Tuesday’s National Election Oct 28, 2026 In Israel, there’s no clear winner so far in Tuesday’s national election. The final tally could take days. It was Israel’s first election since the October 7, 2023, attack and the ensuing wars in Gaza, Lebanon and Iran. With over 70% of the vote counted, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s Likud party leads with 27 seats, ahead of former military chief Gadi Eisenkot’s Yashar party at 22. Neither candidate is on track to form a governing majority of 61 seats in the Knesset. According to Haaretz, a possible pro-Netanyahu coalition currently has 54 seats, while a possible pro-Eisenkot bloc has 49 seats. Palestinian parties — the Joint List and Ra’am — have won 17 seats, their strongest showing ever. But both Netanyahu and Eisenkot have ruled out governing with Palestinian-led parties. Meanwhile, millions of Palestinians living under Israeli occupation in East Jerusalem, the West Bank and Gaza were ineligible to vote. This is Netanyahu speaking on Tuesday. > Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu: “We must form a right-wing, national, strong government. That is what must be done. We must not — must not — endanger Israel and establish a government that is backed by anti-Zionist Arab parties.”

Lancet Calls for Global Climate Health Emergency (Health) Israel’s general election has left both Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s coalition and former military chief Gadi Eisenkot’s opposition bloc without a parliamentary majority, according to exit polls. Two broadcasters projected both blocs winning 51 seats in the 120-seat Knesset, while another gave Netanyahu a narrow lead. Both leaders claimed victory as counting continued. ... The two Arab parties are projected to secure a record 18 or 19 seats, potentially determining who can form a government. However, only one opposition party has openly supported working with them and a unity government between Netanyahu and Eisenkot also appears unlikely. Turnout reached 77.7%, its highest level at that stage since 1999. Around 600,000 absentee ballots, mostly from military personnel, will not be fully counted until Thursday. Once results are confirmed, Israel’s president will consult political factions before selecting a leader to attempt forming a coalition, a process that could take weeks. Another election remains possible. Finnish President Alexander Stubb and Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Stoere held a rare 90-minute telephone call with Russian President Vladimir Putin on Tuesday, urging an end to the war in Ukraine. They subsequently spoke with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky. The initiative preceded planned talks involving Russia, Ukraine and the United States in Abu Dhabi next month. The outreach exposed divisions among European leaders. Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen criticised the lack of coordination and said she saw no signs Russia wanted peace. Swedish Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson warned against dividing Europe’s position, while Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha welcomed the contact as coordinated with Kyiv. The Kremlin offered no indication of compromise, insisting Russia’s interests must be fully considered. The call followed US President Donald Trump’s shift towards Russia, including purchases of Russian diesel and eased sanctions. Stubb and Stoere said they acted for their own countries, not Europe. ... Brazilian Supreme Court Justice Flávio Dino has ordered a police investigation into possible illegal foreign assistance to Flávio Bolsonaro’s presidential campaign, following his defeat by President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva on Sunday. Investigators will examine alleged contacts involving the Rockbridge Network, a US donor group co-founded by Vice President JD Vance, and Brazilian intermediaries. Brazilian law prohibits foreign campaign funding and other economic assistance. The allegations arose from complaints by Bolsonaro’s opponents, including former presidential candidate Renan Santos. Rockbridge denied involvement, saying Brazilians claiming to represent the network had falsely presented themselves as its agents. Dino emphasised that the investigation did not establish wrongdoing. ... The Pentagon has put the cost of the US war against Iran at $47.1 billion through 16 October, with munitions accounting for more than 60% of spending. The figure exceeds Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth’s July estimate of $37.5 billion by more than 25%, even as President Donald Trump holds back from restarting major combat operations. ... The European Commission is proposing rules requiring member states to prepare for a 3C rise in global temperatures by 2100 and identify which authorities are responsible for managing climate risks. EU Climate Commissioner Wopke Hoekstra said cutting emissions alone would not protect citizens from increasingly severe heatwaves, floods and wildfires. Europe is warming at roughly twice the global average. The proposals would bring climate scenarios into decisions on infrastructure and public investment. Hoekstra estimated that extreme weather caused more than €100 billion in economic damage across Europe this summer, while high temperatures contributed to approximately 50,000 deaths. Financing remains a central gap. The Commission estimates that adaptation will require €70 billion annually until 2050, but the proposed framework includes no new funding. ... Researchers behind the Lancet Countdown report have called on the World Health Organization and United Nations to declare climate change a global health emergency, warning that health risks are accelerating faster than efforts to address them. The report estimates that heat caused three million deaths worldwide between 2016 and 2023, with 68% attributable to climate change. Heat-related deaths reached a record 710,000 in 2023, more than 70% linked to human-caused warming. The researchers also identified growing risks from drought, extreme rainfall and conditions favouring dengue transmission. They argue that an emergency declaration could strengthen health surveillance, early warnings and coordinated action. The report also estimates that reduced worker productivity from warming has cost the global economy more than $1 trillion annually over the past three years. Lancet Countdown executive director Marina Romanello called for a long-term response rather than successive emergency measures, as climate-related health threats continue to grow.

items.title: Federal Reserve Board - Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement
items.excerpt: ## Press Release October 28, 2026 ### Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement For release at 2:00 p.m. EDT The Federal Open Market Committee approved the following statement for release by a 10 – 2 vote: The Committee decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 3-3/4 to 4 percent, in support of the Federal Reserve's dual mandate. The Committee is continuing its policy of maintaining ample reserves in the banking system. Economic activity is expanding at a strong pace. While uncertainty remains elevated owing, in part, to geopolitical developments, domestic spending has been resilient. Productivity growth is strong, and capital investment is robust. Job gains have kept pace with the workforce, and the unemployment rate has changed little. Inflation remains elevated. The accumulation of more information will help the Committee determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the Committee's 2 percent goal. The Committee will deliver price stability. Voting against the monetary policy action were Lisa D. Cook and Beth M. Hammack, who preferred to raise the target range for the federal funds rate by 1/4 percentage point at this meeting.

items.title: Fed holds interest rates steady despite stubborn inflation : NPR
items.excerpt: The central bank renewed its pledge to deliver price stability, a goal that's been made more difficult by a spike in energy prices tied to the U.S. war with Iran. "Inflation remains elevated," the Fed's rate-setting committee acknowledged in a statement. At its last policy meeting in September, the Fed raised rates for the first time in more than three years. Since then, data has shown inflation has continued to accelerate, with consumer prices in September up 3.7% from a year ago — a bigger annual increase than the previous month. "It's 'wrong way," says Dan North, a senior economist at the insurance company Allianz Trade. "That inflation line is going up, not down." ... ### AI helps prop up the economy Other parts of the economy are less sensitive to rising interest rates. The booming investment in artificial intelligence, for example, shows no sign of slowing down, no matter how much the Fed tries to tap on the brakes. "The A.I. companies don't care what interest rate they have to pay," North says. The frenzied push to build A.I. data centers is pushing up prices for construction materials and electronic equipment. That's not the case for less wealthy families, whose wages are not keeping pace with the rising cost of living. Average wages rose just 3% for the 12 months ending in September. "Lower and middle-income Americans are having a real struggle," says Mark Zandi, chief economist at Moody's Analytics. " Their purchasing power is actually declining. And that's a pretty uncomfortable place to be. And that likely goes to explain to a large degree why people don't feel very good about the economy."

items.title: Inflation worsened last month to 3.7% as midterm elections ...
items.excerpt: Economy Oct 14, 2026 9:37 AM EDT WASHINGTON (AP) — U.S. inflation accelerated last month as gas, clothes, and air fares got more expensive, evidence that rising prices remain an economic challenge just a few weeks before the midterm elections that have focused heavily on issues related to affordability. The consumer price index rose 3.7% in September compared with a year ago, the Labor Department said Wednesday, up from 3.4% in August. On a monthly basis, costs jumped 0.6% from August to September, the biggest gain in five months, up from a 0.4% increase the previous month. The figures underscore the lingering impact of the Iran war on gas prices and the stubborn persistence of inflation, which fell sharply from a 9.1% peak in 2022 but this year has ticked higher since the war began in late February. The rise isn't all linked to gas prices, as surging investment in data centers and AI has also pushed up prices for computer chips and the consumer electronics that also use them. Elevated inflation has posed political problems for Republicans in Congress and is a challenge for the Federal Reserve, which is required by Congress to seek stable prices. Excluding the volatile food and energy categories, core prices rose 2.6% in September from a year ago, up from 2.4% the previous month. And they climbed 0.3% from August to September, an elevated pace that, if it continued for a year, would run well above the Fed's 2% target. ... By raising borrowing costs, the Fed hopes to slow spending and growth and cool price increases. Yet much of the current inflation comes from supply shocks, such as the Iran war's disruption to oil and gas supplies, and higher interest rates can't address those bottlenecks. Warsh has said his goal is to keep the gas price spike from seeping into more areas of the economy. It's already pushed up the price of air fares about 22% from a year ago. ... Gas prices jumped more than 9% from August to September, Wednesday's report said. Rising gas costs are a highly visible sign of inflation and often drive down measures of consumer sentiment about the economy. Prices at the pump have ticked lower in the past two weeks to a nationwide average of $4.33 a gallon, according to AAA, though they remain higher than a month ago.

items.excerpt: October 28, 2026, 10:09 PM EDT By NBC News ## What to know today - TRUMP TO OHIO: President Donald Trump held a rally in Ohio today in one of the most notable battleground states of the cycle, where recent polling shows both the Senate and the governor’s races are close. - CALIFORNIA BALLOTS: A federal judge in California today refused a request by the Trump administration to segregate 20,000 mail-in ballots from people it alleges are noncitizens. - OBAMA HEADS TO GEORGIA: Former President Barack Obama held a rally in Georgia today with the Democratic candidates for the Senate and governor. Democratic Sen. Jon Ossoff has been leading Republican Rep. Mike Collins in recent polls, while Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms is running a close race against Republican Rick Jackson in the governor's contest. - CHOOSING NEITHER: Fewer of America’s youngest voters are choosing to register as Democratic or Republican compared with similar cohorts in previous midterm elections, an NBC News analysis of TargetSmart voter registration data found. ... ## Judge declines to block California from counting alleged noncitizen voters’ ballots in DOJ lawsuit A federal judge in California today refused a request by the Trump administration to segregate 20,000 mail-in ballots from people it alleges are noncitizens. “This request violates longstanding constitutional principles mandating that states have control over their elections,” U.S. District Judge David Carter wrote. “If Plaintiff’s last-minute request for relief were granted, either party could create chaos for their own political purposes to disrupt the election process.” Carter, as he did during a hearing yesterday, said there is a “clear remedy” available to the federal government: its prosecutorial tools. Carter also noted that California has established procedures to cancel the voter registration of any person proved ineligible. “The Executive’s requested relief, however, would wreak havoc and disrupt the election that is already underway, create a chilling effect on election workers and voters alike, and discount the votes of United States citizens,” he wrote. ... ## Trump says Mary Peltola shouldn't be allowed to run for Senate in Alaska Trump said former Rep. Mary Peltola, D-Alaska, should not appear on the ballot in Alaska’s Senate race. “In Alaska, I don’t think Mary Peltola, after perpetrating such a terrible scheme, should be allowed to run, because this is ELECTION FRAUD,” Trump wrote about a report from The New York Times that said aides tied to the Peltola campaign and the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee helped recruit former schoolteacher Dan J. Sullivan to run, potentially creating confusion between him and Republican Sen. Dan S. Sullivan, whom Trump has endorsed. NBC News has not independently confirmed the Times’ reporting. The Times cites Elisa Rios, Peltola’s former campaign manager who spoke on the record for the article and later contacted the paper to retract “all statements made regarding the 2026 Alaska Senate race.” Rios was fired from Peltola's campaign in August. The Justice Department had earlier sued the state of Alaska, seeking to block election results if Dan J. Sullivan draws votes away from Dan S. Sullivan. That case is still in progress.

UK's Channel 4 shows to launch on Disney+ next year Channel 4 has signed a deal with ​The Walt Disney Company to bring its shows to the Disney+ streaming platform in Britain and Ireland ​early next year. The collaboration will see many of Channel 4's programmes, including ‌drama "Maya", ​featuring Bella Ramsey, released on Disney+ at the same time as on Channel 4's own platforms, the broadcaster said on Tuesday. Actor Walter Koenig, 'Star Trek's' plucky Chekov, dies at 90 Walter Koenig, who brought humor and grit to the role of starship navigator Pavel Chekov on the classic 1960s sci-fi TV series "Star Trek" and seven subsequent feature ‌films, has died at the age of 90. "My heart is heavy. Walter Koenig, our Ensign Pavel Chekov, passed away early today," George Takei, who starred alongside Koenig in the show and was a long-time friend, wrote on Facebook on Monday. Koenig died at his home in Los Angeles, the AP reported, citing his talent agent. Meghan to join Australia's Junior MasterChef next year Meghan, the wife of Britain's Prince Harry, will star in the next series of Australia's Junior MasterChef in ‌2027, returning to a franchise where she appeared as a guest judge on the adult version earlier this year. Meghan, an American actress before she married Harry in 2018, has recently moved back to Britain from the US ‌with her family, with media reports suggesting she was keen to find a new acting role. Noah Wyle named People magazine's 'sexiest man alive' Actor Noah Wyle, the Emmy-winning star of the TV medical drama “The Pitt,” was named this year’s “sexiest man alive” by People magazine on Tuesday. The 55-year-old said it “sounded like a prank” when he heard the news, adding: “Not in a million years did I think that this would be an honor bestowed on me.” Universal Music Group discussed going private with buyout firms, Bloomberg News reports Universal Music Group held preliminary discussions with private equity firms earlier ⁠this year ​about going private, Bloomberg News reported on Monday, citing people familiar ⁠with the matter. The music label's management held preliminary talks with private equity firms including Apollo Global Management, TPG and Blackstone, according to the report ... US ⁠singer ​Chris Brown spared immediate jail sentence for UK affray charge US singer Chris Brown was spared an immediate prison sentence in Britain on Monday for attacking a producer with a tequila bottle in a London nightclub in 2023. Brown, 37, was given an eight-month suspended sentence at London's Southwark Crown Court having pleaded guilty to a charge of affray over the attack on Abraham Diaw at the Tape nightclub in February 2023. Macklemore vows to fight until 'last breath' ⁠at opening of 'Free Palestine' tour American rapper Macklemore vowed to continue to speak out loudly against Israel's war in Gaza at the opening of his "Free Palestine" concert tour organised after he was dropped as the opening act for ⁠Ed Sheeran over pro-Palestinian remarks. The Grammy-winning rapper received a deafening ⁠ovation in Dublin, where fans in the overwhelmingly pro-Palestinian country came draped in Palestinian flags, black, red and green football jerseys and keffiyeh scarves being sold by vendors outside.

items.excerpt: - AP - Oct 28, 2026 - Oct 28, 2026 Updated 22 mins ago Ken Burns wins a $250,000 prize for bringing American history to life NEW YORK (AP) — Ken Burns has won a $250,000 prize for his contributions to American history. The New York Historical awarded him the inaugural David M. Rubenstein Prize for the Advancement of American History. The jury praised Burns for his work on topics like the American Revolution and the Civil War. They noted his films have brought the history of the U.S. to more people than perhaps any other single body of work. Burns expressed gratitude, acknowledging the collective effort of historians and archivists. The award was established earlier this year by financier David M. Rubenstein. California appeals court upholds actor Danny Masterson's rape convictions LOS ANGELES (AP) — A California appeals court has upheld actor Danny Masterson’s convictions and long prison sentence for raping two women at his home in 2003. The three-judge panel on Tuesday unanimously found that the “That ’70s Show” actor had failed to demonstrate that the lower court made errors that would warrant granting him a new trial. Masterson was convicted in 2023 of raping two women at his home two decades earlier. He was sentenced to 30 years to life in prison. His attorneys said in an emailed statement Tuesday that they would seek review at the California Supreme Court. Russell Brand denies all charges as he takes the stand at his rape and sex assault trial LONDON (AP) — Russell Brand says allegations of sexual misconduct have had a “devastating” impact on his life. The actor and comedian testified in court Wednesday at his trial on charges of rape and sexual assault. Brand, 51, denied all charges, stating that friends and colleagues have abandoned him. He also mentioned being barred from staying with his baby son in the hospital due to the allegations. Over the past two weeks, prosecutors have presented their case, with six women accusing Brand of misconduct between 1999 and 2009. Brand insists that consent is fundamental, denying any wrongdoing. Iran sentences acclaimed film director Jafar Panahi to new prison term after his return home CAIRO (AP) — Iran has sentenced acclaimed film director Jafar Panahi to five years and one month in prison, following his return to the country earlier this year, after the start of U.S. and Israeli attacks on the Islamic Republic. The Tehran court also ordered the confiscation of Panahi’s “movable and immovable assets.” That's according to his lawyer Mostafa Nili, who spoke in an interview with the reformist news site Emtedad on Tuesday. Nili did not say what Panahi was convicted of. But the director, who returned to Iran in March, had been previously convicted of “propaganda activities against the system.” Susan Saint James, Emmy-winning actor of 'McMillan & Wife' and 'Kate & Allie,' dies at 80 LOS ANGELES (AP) — Susan Saint James, known for her roles in “McMillan & Wife” and “Kate & Allie,” has died at 80. People magazine reports she passed away Monday after a battle with pancreatic cancer. Born in Los Angeles, she started modeling in Paris as a teenager and later signed with Universal Studios. She gained fame in the 1970s and 1980s, earning multiple Emmy nominations. Saint James retired to focus on family but occasionally appeared on TV. She was a longtime supporter of the Special Olympics and leaves behind her husband, children, and extended family. Taylor Swift, Lyle Lovett and more inducted into Nashville Songwriters Hall of Fame NASHVILLE, Tenn. (AP) — Taylor Swift has been inducted into the Nashville Songwriters Hall of Fame, alongside Lyle Lovett, Shawn Camp, Lee Thomas Miller, Bruce Channel and J.I. Allison. Swift signed her first publishing deal in Nashville at the age of 14. She returned to the city on Monday during the Nashville Songwriters Hall of Fame annual gala celebration. She said it was an incredible honor to be inducted and described soaking up the lessons from other writers like a sponge. Also honored was country music icon George Strait with the organization's Career Maker Award. He said the songwriters helped to make his career. Jay-Z picks himself to headline the Super Bowl halftime show at SoFi Stadium in Southern California LOS ANGELES (AP) — Jay-Z will headline the Super Bowl halftime show on Feb. 14 at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California. The NFL, Apple Music, and Roc Nation announced the news Monday night. NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell said he always wanted Jay-Z to perform when the time felt right. Jay-Z expressed excitement about the opportunity, calling it a dream come true. His Roc Nation has partnered with the NFL since 2019 to produce entertainment presentations, including the halftime show. Jay-Z, who has won 25 Grammy Awards, will perform at the stadium where he recently celebrated the 30th anniversary of his debut album, “Reasonable Doubt.” Andrea Bocelli concerts in Indonesia to proceed despite opposition from Muslim clerics JAKARTA, Indonesia (AP) — Italian tenor Andrea Bocelli's concerts in Indonesia will proceed despite opposition from the country's top Muslim clerical body. The Indonesian Ulema Council demanded the cancellation due to Bocelli's past support for Israel. Indonesia, a strong supporter of Palestinians, does not have formal diplomatic relations with Israel. The concerts are scheduled for October 31 at Borobudur Temple and November 3 in Jakarta. Promoter Shoemaker Live insists the events will support Indonesia's tourism and culture sectors. Bocelli plans to dedicate songs to humanity and world peace. The council argues the concerts could hurt Indonesians who support Palestinians. After pushback, the Dutch reverse course and withdraw from Eurovision again AMSTERDAM (AP) — The Netherlands is withdrawing from participating in the Eurovision Song Contest, reversing a decision in September to return to the show. NPO, the umbrella organization for public broadcasters in the country announced in September it would send a performer to the event, after a subsidiary had said a month earlier it would boycott the contest for a second year. Earlier this month, hundreds of NPO employees sent a letter opposing Dutch participation. A number of prominent Dutch media personalities also publicly objected to the move.
